system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

5 EU-Alert capabilities 5.1 Language The need to support Public Warning Messages in various languages is necessary for the European Public Warning System because there are many European countries that share borders where there is a frequent and significant movement of mobile subscribers across those borders, i.e. a high instance of international roaming. Emergency messages should be sent out to users in their own language but when not practicable, then in the language of the message originator. It is impractical to determine the language of the user and so messages shall be sent out in the native language of the country originating the message and subject to national requirements, in any other language or languages that the originator chooses. A CBS structure is required to accommodate the requirement to broadcast messages in multiple languages virtually simultaneously in order not to disadvantage any recipient of a message in a particular language. ETSI TS 123 041 [1] contains an assignment of Message Identifiers for EU-Alert messages in the local language, which is the same range as for CMAS messages in English. This range of Message Identifiers shall be used when the national requirements demand that the UE receive and display the EU-Alert messages in local languages unconditionally.

data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. The English text fits on one GSM-7 page. The Arabic text does not: it is 93 UCS-2 characters, which comes to 3 pages, but the UAE handset advice limits messages to 1 page. A UCS-2 page carries 82 octets, about 41 Arabic characters. The first Arabic page holds the exercise label, the hazard and the start of the action ('قُد'). The rest of the action ('بحذر') and the area/time fall onto later pages. The drafter can fix this by shortening the Arabic text.

objections.issue: The Arabic text is 93 UCS-2 characters and spans 3 cell broadcast pages, but UAE handset advice limits messages to 1 page. In UCS-2, one 82-octet page holds about 41 characters. As drafted, the action is split across pages 1 and 2, and the affected areas and end time ('until 18:00') are on later pages that some handsets may not display together.
objections.fix: Shorten the Arabic to no more than 41 UCS-2 characters so it fits on one page. Keep the exercise label, the hazard and the full action. One option, about 38 characters: 'تمرين: غبار ورؤية أقل من 3 كم. قد بحذر'. Dropping the diacritic on 'قُد' saves one character. If the area and end time must appear in Arabic, someone needs to decide which content to cut, because it cannot all fit on one page.

no_basis.concern: The 1-page limit comes from a summary of the UAE handset spec. None of the clauses shown is the UAE national rule that would set this limit as binding.
